body: CHIEF RECONCILIATION RECORD — two legacy abandoned rows are to be converted to landed_out_of_band, not treated as governed landings and not exempted by checker prose. Exact current-main evidence: cand-4TB2H58FZP5EYF8W8TTCMJ4EAJ is commit 220cbdcc23274ffd42206e53b56fcd042925ee17 and appears as a non-merge commit on the first-parent line; cand-66YCE7XWGG0Q90GNPWR6XM191H is commit e022c5f01aff45c9507656ce2735a9f6cbc5faa3 and also appears as a non-merge first-parent commit. Their accepted abandonment ops 20260830T022535.848606Z-p89333-c0000-re71c-hde4298 and 20260830T022538.265204Z-p89348-c0000-rbf92-h98a1d2 explicitly say the commits were already in main but that a retroactive landed op would misstate missing review, authorization, and landing. That reasoning was correct under the old state vocabulary. The newly installed audited Mote provides candidate reconcile, whose landed_out_of_band state now records the missing distinction: Git contains the exact candidate while governance was bypassed. I will use exact phase CAS, target main, Git reachability proof, and operator override on these two rows only. This does not grant or fabricate review or authorization, does not validate the historical bypass, and does not change source. It repairs the ledger so the premerge checker can continue to reject pending, abandoned, superseded, ambiguous, and malformed first-parent candidates while accepting only actual landed or explicitly reconciled history.
